With no tickets to work from, I should escalate to legal as P2 since this involves Breathing Space and a payment plan needing human review. I'll note there's no tool to cancel scheduled actions, but since the tenant initiated contact, replying with an acknowledgment is permitted without chasing arrears, and I should route communication to the debt adviser since a third party is formally involved.

Landlord notification is fine too, since they're the creditor rather than a data subject here. So my actions are: escalate, message the tenant, message the adviser, message the landlord, add a note, and schedule a follow-up — with Breathing Space running 60 days from October 1st, ending around November 30th.

It has been passed to a colleague and to your landlord, and any reply will go through your adviser. Your normal rent is still due, and repairs carry on as usual. Please contact us about anything on that side. Kind regards, Mare & Co Lettings

answers.question: 1. What legal constraint applies and what can't you do?
answers.answer: A standard Breathing Space started 01/10/2026 (about 60 days, end date to confirm). We must stop all arrears contact and enforcement, so no arrears chaser SMS, no Section 8 or Ground 8 notice or draft, and no court steps. Contact with the debtor about the debt happens through the adviser, except where the debtor starts it. Current rent stays payable and repair contact continues.

answers.question: 2. Can you accept the proposed payment plan?
answers.answer: No. Payment plans need human and landlord authority. I acknowledged the offer without accepting or refusing it. At £100 a month it would take about 37 months to clear £3,700, on top of the rent. It is being reviewed via legal, the landlord and the adviser.

answers.question: 3. What actions and communications, to whom?
answers.answer: Acknowledged the tenant by email (A2). Emailed adviser Ruth Okoye (A3). Told landlord Ben Hartley (A4). Added a note to the tenant record to stop arrears actions (A5). Escalated to legal P2 (A1). Scheduled a 12 Oct check that the SMS and Section 8 review were cancelled (A6).

With no tickets to work from, I should escalate to legal as P2 since this involves Breathing Space and a payment plan needing human review. I'll note there's no tool to cancel scheduled actions, but since the tenant initiated contact, replying with an acknowledgment is permitted without chasing arrears, and I should route communication to the debt adviser since a third party is formally involved.

Landlord notification is fine too, since they're the creditor rather than a data subject here. So my actions are: escalate, message the tenant, message the adviser, message the landlord, add a note, and schedule a follow-up — with Breathing Space running 60 days from October 1st, ending around November 30th.

arguments.body: Hi Daniel, thanks for your email and the letter from your debt adviser. We have it and have noted your Breathing Space. We won't chase you about the arrears while it runs, and we'll deal with that through Ruth Okoye at Hackney Money Advice. I can't accept or turn down your £100 a month offer myself. It has been passed to a colleague and to your landlord, and any reply will go through your adviser. Your normal rent is still due, and repairs carry on as usual. Please contact us about anything on that side. Kind regards, Mare & Co Lettings

Dear Ruth, we have received the Breathing Space notice (ref HMA-55102, start 01/10/2026) for Daniel Reyes, Flat 3, 8 Kingsland Road. We have stopped arrears contact and enforcement activity and will deal with you on the debt. Mr Reyes has offered £100 a month on top of rent from November. That offer is with our team and the landlord for review. We will reply to you, not to him. Please confirm the end date of the breathing space. Regards, Mare & Co Lettings

Hi Ben, the tenant at Flat 3, 8 Kingsland Road has sent a Breathing Space notice from his debt adviser, effective 01/10/2026. While it runs we must stop all arrears contact and enforcement, and we can't serve or prepare arrears notices. He has offered £100 a month extra from November. I haven't accepted it; our team will come back to you with options. His current rent is still due. Regards, Mare & Co Lettings

details.summary: Tenant admitted £3,700 arrears and offered £100/month; his attached notice shows a standard Breathing Space from 01/10/2026. I stopped all arrears activity, acknowledged the tenant, informed the adviser and landlord, noted the record and escalated to legal to cancel the scheduled SMS and Section 8 review.

answers.question: 1. What legal constraint applies and what can't you do?
answers.answer: A standard Breathing Space started 01/10/2026 (about 60 days, end date to confirm). We must stop all arrears contact and enforcement, so no arrears chaser SMS, no Section 8 or Ground 8 notice or draft, and no court steps. Contact with the debtor about the debt happens through the adviser, except where the debtor starts it. Current rent stays payable and repair contact continues.

answers.question: 2. Can you accept the proposed payment plan?
answers.answer: No. Payment plans need human and landlord authority. I acknowledged the offer without accepting or refusing it. At £100 a month it would take about 37 months to clear £3,700, on top of the rent. It is being reviewed via legal, the landlord and the adviser.

answers.question: 3. What actions and communications, to whom?
answers.answer: Acknowledged the tenant by email (A2). Emailed adviser Ruth Okoye (A3). Told landlord Ben Hartley (A4). Added a note to the tenant record to stop arrears actions (A5). Escalated to legal P2 (A1). Scheduled a 12 Oct check that the SMS and Section 8 review were cancelled (A6).
